etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English whoever. By surface analysis, who +‎ ever.

definitions.definition: (interrogative) Who ever: an emphatic form of who.
(fused relative) Any person or persons that.
(fused relative) The person that (no matter who).
Regardless of the person or persons that.
Misspelling of who ever other than in interrogative use.

quote.citation: 2014 July 13, Peter FitzSimons, “Ian Thorpe acknowledges he's gay, let's hope he's now happy as well”, in Sydney Morning Herald:
quote.text: When the gays can claim the toughest bastard whoever pulled on a football boot as one of their own, ...
